title: Mali Federation Formed with French Sudan
notes: Mali Federation founded 4 April 1959. Senghor led Senegal's participation; Modibo Keita headed federation. Confirmed by Wikipedia and Britannica.

title: Independence from France and Mali Federation Collapse
notes: Independence within federation 20 June 1960; Senegal withdrew and declared full independence 20 August 1960. Senghor first president, Mamadou Dia PM. All facts confirmed.

title: Senghor Inaugurates African Socialist Development Model
notes: Senghor's African socialism ideology and groundnut-centred development plans are well-documented in historical sources.

title: Coup Attempt by Prime Minister Mamadou Dia Suppressed
notes: Crisis peaked 17 December 1962. Dia ordered army to lock assembly building; Senghor declared coup attempt and had Dia arrested 18 December. Sentenced to life imprisonment May 1963. Confirmed by multiple sources.

title: New Constitution Establishes Presidential System
notes: Constitution Law 63-22 of 7 March 1963 abolished parliamentary system and prime minister post, established presidential republic. Confirmed by ConstitutionNet.

title: De Facto Single-Party State Established
notes: UPS declared sole party in 1966; opposition absorbed or suppressed. Confirmed by multiple political history sources.

title: Student and Worker Uprising Shakes Senghor Government
notes: Students struck 27 May 1968; UNTS called general strike; Senghor declared state of emergency. French troops intervened. All facts confirmed.

title: Prime Minister Position Restored, Abdou Diouf Appointed
notes: Diouf appointed PM 26 February 1970 after Senghor reinstated the post. Confirmed by Wikipedia and Britannica.

title: Groundnut Crisis and Drought Devastate Rural Economy
notes: Sahelian drought and oil shock affected Senegal's groundnut economy in the early 1970s; IMF involvement well-documented.

title: Controlled Multiparty System Introduced
notes: Three-party limited system introduced 1974; PDS founded July 1974. Confirmed by multiple sources. Note: event description says 'three parties' but sources indicate some flexibility.

title: Full Multiparty System Restored
notes: UPS renamed PS in December 1976 and PDS was already legal since 1974. However, full unrestricted multiparty competition was not restored until 1981 per sources — not 1976. The 1976 change expanded from 3 to 4 ideological slots but was still a controlled system. Description overstates the openness.

title: First Genuinely Contested Presidential Elections Held
notes: Wade won 17.38% against Senghor in February 1978 election. Facts confirmed by Wikipedia election article.

title: Senghor Voluntarily Transfers Power to Diouf
notes: Senghor resigned 31 December 1980, transferring to Diouf. First modern African leader to resign voluntarily. Confirmed by multiple sources. Note: transfer happened 1 January 1981, not 31 December 1980 per some sources, but Senghor signed resignation 31 Dec.

title: Casamance Separatist Movement Begins Armed Insurgency
notes: Year is off. The event description assigns year 1981 but correctly states inside the text that the armed insurgency began in December 1982 (first demonstration 26 December 1982). The armed wing Atika was not formed until 1985. Year field should be 1982.

title: Senegalese Military Intervenes to Restore Gambian Government
notes: Coup attempt by Kukoi Samba Sanyang on 30 July 1981; ~2,700 Senegalese troops deployed. Jawara invoked 1967 Mutual Defense Agreement. Confirmed by Wikipedia.

title: Senegambia Confederation Established with The Gambia
notes: Agreement signed 17 December 1981, entered into force 1 February 1982. Dissolved 30 September 1989. Confirmed by Wikipedia.

title: IMF Structural Adjustment Reforms Implemented
notes: IMF structural adjustment in early 1980s well-documented for Senegal. Year 1983 is plausible and consistent with literature.

title: Casamance Peace Negotiations Collapse, Violence Escalates
notes: Atika armed wing formed 1985; escalation of violence in mid-1980s confirmed. Details broadly consistent with historical record.

title: Post-Election Violence After Disputed Presidential Poll
notes: Election 28 February 1988; Diouf won; riots erupted; state of emergency declared. Wade arrested. All facts confirmed by Wikipedia and UPI archives.

title: Mauritanian-Senegalese Border Crisis and Ethnic Violence
notes: Clashes began April 1989 over grazing rights. Hundreds killed, tens of thousands expelled from both sides. Diplomatic relations severed August 1989, restored May 1992 (border reopened). Event says 1992 restoration — confirmed correct.

title: Senegambia Confederation Dissolved
notes: Dissolved 30 September 1989 after Gambia refused deeper integration. Confirmed by Wikipedia.

title: Casamance Ceasefire Agreement Signed
notes: Ceasefire signed 31 May 1991 in Cacheu, Guinea-Bissau by Sidi Badji and Defence Minister Medoune Fall. Confirmed by Casamance conflict sources. Event says 'mediated by Catholic diocese of Ziguinchor' — location was Cacheu, Guinea-Bissau, not Ziguinchor, but minor detail.

title: CFA Franc Devaluation Triggers Economic Shock
notes: CFA franc devalued 12 January 1994 by 50%. Immediate inflation, IMF-World Bank package. All facts confirmed.

title: Urban Protests Over Austerity and Living Costs
notes: Post-devaluation protests in Dakar well-documented in academic literature.

title: Abdoulaye Wade Joins Government as Minister of State
notes: Wade rejoined government as Minister of State in March 1995; left again in March 1998. Confirmed by Wikipedia.

title: Decentralization Reform Transfers Powers to Local Governments
notes: Code des collectivites locales enacted under Diouf in 1996 is well-documented in Senegal governance literature.

title: Casamance Conflict Intensifies with Cross-Border Guinea-Bissau Dimension
notes: MFDC-Guinea-Bissau nexus and Senegal's 1998-99 intervention in Guinea-Bissau civil war confirmed in conflict literature.

title: Abdoulaye Wade Defeats Diouf in Historic Democratic Transition
notes: First round 27 February 2000; runoff 19 March 2000. Wade won runoff with 58.49%. Senegal's first democratic alternance. All facts confirmed.

title: New Constitution Approved by Referendum
notes: Referendum 7 January 2001; approved by ~94% of voters. Reduced term from 7 to 5 years; abolished Senate. Confirmed by Wikipedia and ConstitutionNet.

title: Le Joola Ferry Disaster Kills Over 1,800 People
notes: MV Le Joola capsized 26 September 2002 off Gambia coast; 1,863 deaths confirmed. Ship carried over 3x capacity. Facts confirmed. Note: category listed as 'flood_and_cyclone' is incorrect (should be maritime disaster), but factual content is accurate.

title: Senegal Reaches HIPC Debt Relief Completion Point
notes: Year is wrong. Senegal reached HIPC completion point in April 2004, not 2002. The $850 million figure is correct. Year off by 2 years = FALSE.

title: World Cup Appearance — Senegal Defeats France
notes: Senegal's first World Cup appearance in 2002 Korea/Japan. Defeated defending champion France 1-0 (Papa Bouba Diop goal). Reached quarterfinals. All facts confirmed.

title: Senegal Deploys Troops to UN Peacekeeping Missions
notes: Senegal is a long-standing top African UN peacekeeping contributor. Year 2003 is a reasonable date for consolidation; facts are broadly accurate.

title: Casamance Peace Agreement Signed in Ziguinchor
notes: Peace agreement signed 30-31 December 2004 in Ziguinchor; all MFDC factions including Atika validated it. Implementation partial. Confirmed by Peace Accords Matrix and Wikipedia.

title: Senegal Hosts African Union Summit — Dakar Becomes Continental Hub
notes: Could not confirm a specific African Union Summit hosted by Dakar in 2006. The AU Summits in 2006 were held in Khartoum (January) and Banjul (July). Wade's continental role and NEPAD involvement are documented but no Dakar AU summit in 2006 confirmed.

title: Wade Re-elected in First-Round Presidential Victory
notes: Wade won 55.9% in first round on 25 February 2007. Opposition contested result. All facts confirmed by Wikipedia.

title: Food Price Crisis Sparks Urban Protests
notes: Global food price crisis 2008 affected Senegal, with rice prices rising sharply. Urban protests documented. Facts consistent with regional literature.

title: Idrissa Seck Corruption Case and Factional Conflicts Intensify
notes: Seck was detained in pretrial detention 2005-2006 (not 2009). Charges were dropped. The 2009 date is not supported — the main Seck case events were 2005-2006. The description assigns the year 2009 but the events described happened earlier.

title: Senegal Joins African Peer Review Mechanism
notes: Senegal participated in APRM process; year 2010 is plausible for assessment publication. Facts broadly consistent with APRM documentation.

title: Wade Attempts to Run Son for Vice Presidency
notes: June 2011 constitutional amendment proposed 25% first-round threshold and vice-presidential post widely seen as vehicle for Karim Wade. Y'en a Marre protests forced withdrawal. Constitutional court advised against. All facts confirmed.

title: Third-Term Controversy and Constitutional Court Ruling
notes: Constitutional Council ruled Wade's first term did not count toward two-term limit. Mass protests, deaths, M23 coalition. West African leaders involved. All facts confirmed.

title: Macky Sall Defeats Wade in Presidential Runoff
notes: Runoff 25 March 2012; Sall won 65.8% vs Wade 34.2%. Wade conceded promptly. Confirmed by France 24 and Wikipedia.

title: Karim Wade Arrested on Enrichment Charges
notes: Arrested April 2013; convicted March 2015; sentenced to 6 years + $230 million fine. Pardoned 2016, left for Qatar. All facts confirmed.

title: Senegal Joins ECOWAS Force Against Gambian Crisis
notes: The ECOWAS military intervention in Gambia against Jammeh occurred in January 2017, not 2014. Senegal did play a regional role regarding Gambia throughout the period, but the described ECOWAS force is the 2017 intervention. Year and framing are inaccurate for 2014.

title: Ebola Containment Success Despite Regional Outbreak
notes: Single case confirmed 29 August 2014; no secondary transmission; WHO declared Senegal Ebola-free 17 October 2014. All facts confirmed by WHO sources.

title: Constitutional Referendum Reduces Presidential Term to Five Years
notes: Referendum 20 March 2016; approved 62% of voters; 15 amendments including presidential term reduction. Senate had been abolished in 2012, not in this referendum (event says 'eliminating the Senate' — minor inaccuracy). Core facts confirmed.

title: Plan Senegal Emergent Launched as Economic Blueprint
notes: Year is wrong. PSE was launched in 2014 (first operational phase 2014-2018), not 2016. Year off by 2 years = FALSE.

title: Offshore Oil and Gas Discoveries Confirmed
notes: BP established Mauritania/Senegal region in 2017 following gas discovery confirmation. Sangomar oil (Woodside/Cairn) and Grand Tortue/Ahmeyim LNG (BP/Kosmos) both confirmed commercially viable around this period. Facts broadly accurate.

title: Sall Re-elected in First-Round Presidential Victory
notes: Sall won 58.27% on 24 February 2019 in first round. Sonko, Seck among opponents. Karim Wade and Khalifa Sall excluded. All facts confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Response Praised Internationally
notes: Senegal's early response, Institut Pasteur rapid test kit, and vaccine manufacturing hub role widely documented. Facts confirmed.

title: Ousmane Sonko Trial Triggers Deadly Protests
notes: Sonko arrested March 2021 on rape charges; protests led to 14 reported deaths (event says 'at least thirteen'). Charges later modified. All facts confirmed.

title: Sangomar Oil Field Development Begins
notes: Woodside (acquired FAR Ltd stake) pressed ahead with Sangomar development in 2022; first oil in June 2024. Facts confirmed.

title: Khalifa Sall and Karim Wade Pardoned for Potential Election Candidacy
notes: Karim Wade was pardoned in June 2016, not 2022. Khalifa Sall was pardoned in September 2019. The 2022 date is not supported by sources for either pardon. The political analysis about conditions preventing candidacy is present in commentary but the year assignment is inaccurate.

title: Senegal Wins Africa Cup of Nations for First Time
notes: Senegal beat Egypt 4-2 on penalties in AFCON final on 6 February 2022 in Cameroon. Sadio Mane scored decisive penalty. First AFCON title. All facts confirmed.

title: Sonko Convicted and PASTEF Dissolved
notes: Sonko convicted June 2023 of 'corrupting youth'; sentenced to 2 years. PASTEF dissolved by government decree July 2023. At least 16 people killed in protests per government (higher figures from opposition/Amnesty). All facts confirmed.

title: Massive Wave of Arrests of Opposition Supporters
notes: Over 1,000 arrests documented by human rights organisations following PASTEF dissolution and protests. Amnesty International and HRW documented abuses. Facts confirmed.

title: Sall Postpones Presidential Election by Decree
notes: Sall signed decree 3 February 2024 postponing 25 February election. ECOWAS and Constitutional Council condemned. First such postponement in Senegal's history. All facts confirmed.

title: Constitutional Council Orders Election to Proceed
notes: Constitutional Council ruled postponement unconstitutional on 15 February 2024. Faye ran as PASTEF's official candidate with Sonko's backing. Facts confirmed.

title: Sonko Released from Prison, Faye Wins Landslide Victory
notes: Faye won 54.28% on 24 March 2024 in first round. Released from prison 10 days before election under amnesty. Youngest elected president in Africa at 44. All facts confirmed.

title: Ousmane Sonko Appointed Prime Minister
notes: Faye appointed Sonko as PM on 3 April 2024 after inauguration on 2 April. Facts confirmed by Al Jazeera and France 24.

title: Groundnut Basin Cooperative System Established
notes: ONCAD (Office National de Cooperation et d'Assistance au Developpement) is well-documented but was established in 1966, not 1963. The groundnut cooperative system predates ONCAD but the year assignment and ONCAD attribution in 1963 are not confirmed by available sources.

title: Cheikh Anta Diop Publishes 'Nations Negres et Culture' Influence Peaks
notes: Year is materially wrong. 'Nations Negres et Culture' was first published in 1954, not 1974. The event title says 'Publishes' but the description says 'influence peaks' in the 1970s. Using 1974 as the year for publication is factually false. The book was published 20 years earlier.

title: Disputed 1993 Presidential Election and Political Violence
notes: Diouf won 58% on 21 February 1993. Babacar Seye (VP of Constitutional Council) assassinated on 15 May 1993. Wade charged but charges later dropped. All facts confirmed.
